title: A common denominator lies in the Jacobson radicals
statement: Let A be a commutative domain (a ring with no zero divisors) with fraction field K (a field containing A in which every element is a quotient of elements of A). Let B_1, ..., B_r be subrings of K that are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], semilocal (having finitely many maximal ideals) domains with fraction field K. Assume that each canonical map A \otimes B_i \to K is surjective. Then there exists a nonzero f\in A such that f^{-1} belongs to the Jacobson radical (the intersection of all maximal ideals) of every B_i.

proof.text: For each i let B'_i be the integral closure of B_i in K. The canonical map A tensor B'_i to K remains surjective because its image contains the image of the already-surjective map A tensor B_i to K. By [lem-sc-semilocal-dim-one-conductor] each B'_i is a semilocal Dedekind domain with fraction field K. It is enough to prove the assertion for the B'_i: suppose x in A is nonzero and x^{-1} lies in the Jacobson radical of every B'_i. Then x^{-1} is a nonzero element of that Jacobson radical, and [lem-sc-semilocal-dim-one-conductor] applied to x^{-1} and y=1 gives n_i>0 with x^{-n_i} in B_i; replacing x by x^N with N=n_1...n_r (which keeps x^{-1} in each Jacobson radical, an ideal) puts x^{-1} in every B_i. Now let m be a maximal ideal of B_i. The inclusion B_i into B'_i is injective and B'_i is integral over B_i, so by lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] there is a prime q of B'_i with q cap B_i = m; let n be a maximal ideal of B'_i containing q. Then n cap B_i is a proper ideal containing m, hence equals m, and x^{-1} in n cap B_i = m. So x^{-1} lies in the Jacobson radical of B_i. Thus we may assume every B_i is a semilocal Dedekind domain.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N5 (varieties-lemma-create-globally-generated), proof, paragraphs beginning 'Let B_i' and 'Thus we may assume'

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-semilocal-dedekind-dvr-reduction] to each semilocal Dedekind B_i: it has finitely many maximal ideals m, each localization (B_i)_m is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K, and an element of K lies in the Jacobson radical of B_i exactly when it lies in the maximal ideal of every (B_i)_m. Since B_i is contained in (B_i)_m, the map A tensor (B_i)_m to K is again surjective. Replacing each B_i by its finitely many localizations therefore reduces the claim to a finite family of discrete valuation rings with fraction field K and surjective maps from A tensor each of them to K: a nonzero f in A whose inverse lies in the maximal ideal of every resulting DVR has f^{-1} in the Jacobson radical of each original B_i.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N5 proof, paragraph 'If B_i is not local'

proof.text: For a single resulting DVR B with normalized valuation v, [lem-sc-dvr-tensor-surjective-negative-valuation] supplies a nonzero x in A with v(x)<0. For finitely many valuations v_1,...,v_r, argue by induction on r. The case r=1 is this base case. For r>1, choose by induction a nonzero x in A with v_i(x)<0 for i<r. If v_r(x)<0 we are done. Otherwise use the base case for v_r to choose nonzero y in A with v_r(y)<0. By [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic], after replacing x by a sufficiently large positive power we have v_i(x)<v_i(y) for every i<r. Then z=x+y has v_i(z)=v_i(x)<0 for i<r and v_r(z)=v_r(y)<0, again by the unequal-value sum rule. Since v_r(x) is nonnegative and v_r(y) is negative, z is nonzero. For a DVR B with normalized valuation v and maximal ideal m_B, an element z of K^\times satisfies z^{-1} in m_B exactly when v(z^{-1})=-v(z)>0, i.e. v(z)<0. Thus z is the required element.
